title: REST
body:
REST is an architectural style for [[API]] design built around **resources as nouns** plus [[HTTP Verb]]s as the actions on them. `GET /reviews/123`, `POST /reviews`, `DELETE /reviews/123` — the URL names a thing, and the method says what to do to it. The anti-pattern it's defined against is verb-named endpoints like `/getReview` or `/createReviewNow`.

Other properties that come with the style: it's stateless (see [[Stateless Protocol]]) — each request carries everything needed to serve it, with no server-side conversational memory; representations are typically [[JSON]]; and standard [[HTTP Status Code]]s carry the outcome rather than a custom status field buried in the body. In practice most "REST APIs" are only loosely RESTful, and that's usually fine — the useful part in an interview is being able to say why nouns-plus-methods is the organising principle.
